questions.question: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">The total number of lone-pairs of electrons in Melamine is :<\/div>$\n$
questions.explanation:
**Question Explanation : Determine the total lone pairs in Melamine.
$ $**Concept: Counting non-bonded valence electrons based on the Lewis structure.
$ $**Solution :
$ $
$ $• Melamine has 6 Nitrogen (N) atoms in total (3 in the ring, 3 in the –NH2 groups).
$ $• Nitrogen is in Group 15 and has 5 valence electrons.
$ $• In the structure, every N atom forms exactly 3 bonds (whether N in the ring or N in –NH2)
$ $• Electrons used in bonding = 3.
$ $• Non-bonded electrons = 5 – 3 = 2 electrons.
$ $• Lone pairs per N atom = 2/2 = 1.
$ $• Total lone pairs = 6 (N atoms) × 1 (LP per N) = 6.
$ $**Final Answer : 6
$ $
